units.summary: handlerEntry's breaker becomes the two-step groupBreaker, and it gains a watches context and cancel function. Reconcile cancels these when the handler is replaced or removed.
units.headline: handlerEntry gains watch context and two-step breaker
units.reason: Struct fields added that drive watch lifecycle and breaker semantics.

Context lifetime and leaks

units.summary: New constructor creates a handlerEntry with a fresh breaker and a cancelable watches context.
units.headline: New constructor creates entry with cancelable watch context
units.reason: Introduces per-entry context lifecycle that governs when watches end.
focus: Context is always cancelled on replace or removal, so there is no leak
Unchanged-key reconcile does not call it

units.summary: servingEntry's breaker type changes to groupBreaker, and it gains the watches context so serving can scope watches.
units.headline: servingEntry carries watches context and new breaker type
units.reason: Internal snapshot struct plumbing, with behavior implemented elsewhere.

units.summary: The router creates a root cancelable watches context at construction, used by closeWatches at shutdown.
units.headline: Router initializes root watches context
units.reason: Simple initialization, with behavior carried by closeWatches.

units.summary: On a changed key, reconcile now replaces the handlerEntry instead of mutating it in place. Retired entries are collected, and their watches end after publish so clients re-watch against the new backend. Removed groups are handled the same way.
units.headline: Reconcile replaces entries and ends retired watches after publish
units.reason: Changes lifecycle and ordering of connection termination on backend changes.
focus: Watches end only after publish
Replacing the entry instead of mutating it does not break other holders of the old pointer
Every retired entry's endWatches gets called

units.summary: publish copies each entry's watches context into the servingEntry snapshot.
